review_method: Capacity rescue after no original root draft was saved: independently read every complete actual source unit in2 Kings9–12, every proposed retained target, and necessary context before curating115 pairs. before.relationship: Repeated destruction formula against Ahab's house
before.rationale: Both oracles announce destruction from Ahab's house of every male who urinates against a wall, both confined and abandoned in Israel. The distinctive supplied formula is retained without replacing its social terms by a different edition's wording.

after.relationship: Repeated destruction formula against Ahab's house
after.rationale: Both oracles announce destruction from Ahab's house using the urinates-against-a-wall and confined-and-abandoned formula. Kings here says every one, while the earlier oracle says every male; the common formula is retained without replacing either supplied expression or certifying a new social classification.

changes.reason: Preserve every one versus every male while retaining the repeated formula.

before.relationship: Same-chapter literary parallel: Jezebel oracle recalled after the burial attempt
before.rationale: The messenger predicts dogs devouring Jezebel and none to bury her; the later attempted burial finds only remnants, and the report explicitly recalls the dog oracle. This does not claim a separately narrated final disposition of every remaining bone.

after.relationship: Same-chapter literary parallel: Jezebel oracle recalled after the burial attempt
after.rationale: The messenger predicts dogs devouring Jezebel and none to bury her; the later attempted burial finds only remnants. The returning party reports its finding, and the following reply explicitly recalls the dog oracle. This does not claim a separately narrated final disposition of every remaining bone.

changes.reason: Distinguish the returning party report from the following reply quoting the oracle.

before.relationship: Explicit recall of Elijah's Jezebel oracle
before.rationale: The report identifies the word through Elijah that dogs would devour Jezebel in Jezreel's portion; the earlier oracle predicts dogs at Jezreel's outer wall. The recalled judgment is explicit while the differing location phrases are not independently harmonized.

after.relationship: Explicit recall of Elijah's Jezebel oracle
after.rationale: The reply after the remains report identifies the word through Elijah that dogs would devour Jezebel in Jezreel's portion; the earlier oracle predicts dogs at Jezreel's outer wall. The recalled judgment is explicit while the differing location phrases are not independently harmonized.

changes.reason: The oracle recall belongs to the reply after the remains report, not the report itself.

before.relationship: Same-chapter literary parallel: garments for Baal's slaves and subsequent inspection
before.rationale: The dresser provides garments for Baal's slaves at Jehu's order; Jehu then addresses those slaves about ensuring only Baal's slaves are present. The consecutive actions concern the same explicitly designated group without assigning an unspoken diagnostic function to the garments or defining Mesthaal independently.

after.relationship: Same-chapter literary parallel: garments for Baal's slaves and subsequent inspection
after.rationale: The dresser provides garments for Baal's slaves at Jehu's order; the next scene includes an instruction to those slaves to ensure only Baal's slaves are present. The consecutive actions concern the same explicitly designated group without independently assigning the later He as speaker, inventing a diagnostic function for the garments, or defining Mesthaal.

changes.reason: The following He after Jehu and Jonadab enter is not independently assigned a named inspection speaker.

before.relationship: Baal's house destroyed in separate Israelite and Judean reforms
before.rationale: Jehu's action tears down Baal's pillars and house and makes latrines; the later people of Judah tear down Baal's house, shatter altars and images, and kill its priest. The particular temple destructions are compared without merging their agents, kingdoms, or added actions.

after.relationship: Baal's house destroyed in separate Israelite and Judean reforms
after.rationale: In Jehu's account Baal's pillars and house are pulled down and it is made latrines; the later notice explicitly names the people of the land entering and pulling down Baal's house, shattering altars and images, and killing its priest. The particular destructions are compared without merging their agents, kingdoms, or added actions or making Jehu personally perform the unnamed group's demolition.

changes.reason: The demolition is narrated with They; do not imply Jehu personally performs each act.

before.relationship: Named father-son succession and later regnal heading
before.rationale: Jehu dies and is buried in Samaria, and Jehoahaz his son succeeds; the later heading names Jehoahaz son of Jehu becoming king in Samaria. Its additional seventeenth-year reign length and Judean synchronism remain that heading's own statements.

after.relationship: Named father-son succession and later regnal heading
after.rationale: Jehu dies and is buried in Samaria, and Jehoahaz his son succeeds; the later heading names Jehoahaz son of Jehu becoming king in Samaria. Its additional seventeen-year reign length and Judean synchronism remain that heading's own statements.

changes.reason: Use the cardinal seventeen-year duration supplied in the target.

before.relationship: Same-chapter literary parallel: changed silver instruction and negative agreement
before.rationale: After the king stops silver from their sales and directs it to the bedek, the priests agree neither to receive silver from the people nor to strengthen the house. Both negative clauses are retained rather than rewritten as a new positive promise to do the repairs themselves.

after.relationship: Same-chapter literary parallel: changed silver instruction and negative agreement
after.rationale: After the king orders that no silver be taken from their sales and directs it for the bedek, the priests agree neither to receive silver from the people nor to strengthen the house. The king's directive and both negative agreement clauses are retained rather than rewritten as an already performed financial stoppage or a new positive promise to do the repairs themselves.

changes.reason: Distinguish the royal financial directive from an independently narrated performed stoppage.

unresolved_candidates.status: pending proposed Ahaziah accession-synchronism equation; no chronology reconciliation credit
unresolved_candidates.reason: The source announces Ahaziah becoming king in Joram of Israel eleventh year; the earlier Kings notice gives the twelfth year. The retained connection is the explicit named accession only. This reverse-direction review adds no solution or independent reconciliation credit to the already unresolved earlier notice.

unresolved_candidates.status: pending proposed identity of financial phases and funds; no financial harmonization credit
unresolved_candidates.reason: Kings forbids making its listed gold or silver temple articles from the collected silver; Chronicles narrates articles made from remaining silver after the work was finished. The supplied restriction and explicitly later remainder are compared as distinct statements. No independent proof equates their complete funding histories or resolves all accounting scope.

unresolved_candidates.status: pending proposed killer-name, family-clause, and count harmonization; no identity or numerical reconciliation credit
unresolved_candidates.reason: The retained partial connection is Joash death, David-city burial, and Amaziah succession. Kings names Jezichar son of Jemuath and Jezebuth with the actual his son Shomer phrase. Chronicles names Zabed son of Samath and Jozabed son of Somaroth, adds national descriptions, then all his sons and the five came against him. Those names, relationships, group scope, and counts remain unresolved rather than normalized.
